metadata.description: Foundry build (forge build) — pinned solc per foundry.toml; unique target name so the workspace-wide `-t build test` CI line never runs it without forge
Foundry unit tests (local, deterministic, no network); unique target name (see forge-build)
forge fmt check (no writes in CI)

Slither static analysis; high/medium findings fail (triage baseline: slither.config.json + SLITHER_TRIAGE.md); then the never-triage guard asserts slither.db.json records none of the eight T21 §5.3 detectors

Fork tests against real Base RPC — label-gated in CI + nightly only (never default CI). UNIT-ONLY by ruling (Main, fork round 31949753694): the 256x128 invariant campaigns saturate a keyless public RPC (HTTP 429) — they run locally on anvil via forge-test, and move to fork only with a keyed RPC in the nightly deep campaign. The invariant funding fix stays: future forked invariant runs must not die in setup. Retry/backoff (500ms initial) absorbs public-RPC rate-limit blips [F5]. Optional FORK_BLOCK_BASE pins the block (release-gate B_pin policy, runbook §5: artifact valid only at its recorded block; unset = latest).

Fork tests against Base Sepolia (84532) — wave-5 rehearsal stage 1 (runbook §3, Main ruling): the full unit-only suite is chain-agnostic (deploys into forked state; no venue dependency), proven 49/49 keyless. Nightly + release-tag only; same unit-only/invariant exclusion and B_pin env pattern as fork-test. Stage 2 (Robinhood Chain 46630) lands by ruling once the user RPC arrives.

Fork tests against Robinhood Chain testnet (46630) — wave-6 rehearsal stage 2 (Main wave-6 opening: user RPC delivered, chainId verified live 0xb626). Same chain-agnostic unit-only suite, proven 56/56 keyless against the delivered RPC. Nightly + release-tag only; same unit-only/invariant exclusion and B_fork env pattern as fork-test/fork-test-sepolia.
Validate deploy manifests (fail-closed: missing verificationId = invalid)
RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalizer self-test — the pinned zero-dep tool that produces the G5 artifact contentHash input (runbook §9). Vectors embedded; fail = G5 hashing is broken.

Tier F G1 (runbook Appendix A): unit suite + DEEP invariant campaigns (runs 2048 x depth 512 via [profile.battery.invariant]) — the release-tag battery's stateful evidence. Long-running by design (32x embryo volume); release-tag.yml should give it a generous timeout.

One DEEP invariant campaign at a time (release-tag parallel split, Main ruling): GitHub-hosted jobs hard-cap at 360 minutes and the four campaigns in a single g1 run exceed it. release-tag.yml fans out one job per campaign via INVARIANT_CAMPAIGN (exact invariant_* function name); each job lands far under the cap, wall-clock drops to the slowest campaign, and a counterexample in one campaign no longer buries the others' evidence. battery-g1 stays the single-process aggregate for local/nightly use. Proven: --match-test isolates one campaign (bondParams, 1 test).
Tier F G2 (runbook §4): static analysis (slither --fail-medium + never-triage guard) + the exact selector-surface gate — the structural surface is frozen at the release tag.

Tier F G3 (runbook §5): keyless fork scenarios (FK-1/3/4/5 — FK-6 is a Tier D Blockscout ops step, NOT part of any fork run) against Base Sepolia rehearsal RPC — unit-only by the standing 429 ruling; retry/backoff absorbs public-RPC blips [F5]; FORK_BLOCK_BASE_SEPOLIA pins the FORK state (B_fork; B_pin is the Tier D deploy block), unset = latest. Keyless: no signing, no keys.

Tier F battery wrapper — the ONE canonical entry point for release-tag.yml (npx nx run @kryptr/contracts:battery): G1 deep invariant + G2 static/surface + G3 keyless fork. Tier F PASS at the release tag = wave-5 closing evidence; G4 live + G5 artifact + manifest are wave-6 carry-over (runbook §8).
